nodes.label: PostHog query-cache slice
nodes.intent: An isolated source slice, not the complete PostHog application. Two explicitly adopted promises share one original production oracle.
nodes.why: Use unchanged source to test catalog adoption without altering the working application. The separate pinned runtime runs the original oracle against real Redis and fake S3.

nodes.label: Redis connection factory
nodes.intent: Selects and constructs the query-cache Redis client. No catalog promise is adopted here in this slice.
nodes.why: Retain this real ownership seam without inventing a guarantee from an import or a passing neighboring test.

nodes.label: Query cache
nodes.intent: Stores query results inline in Redis, moves large compressed results to object storage, and conditionally publishes their pointers.
nodes.prose: The cache remains readable while uploads complete asynchronously. Redis byte comparisons arbitrate which upload may publish; the losing upload cleans up its own blob.
nodes.why: A delayed upload must not damage the state that won while it was in flight. Retry recognition is separate from supersession: one distinguishes this operation from a competitor, the other recognizes this operation's own completed effect.
invariants: a late upload cannot replace the newer cache entry or retain its losing blob
repeating an already-installed pointer swap returns success
refutations: a late upload cannot replace the newer cache entry or retain its losing blob: R3 removed the Lua expected-value refusal; the original oracle failed at two retained fake-storage objects instead of one. Restoring it passed.
repeating an already-installed pointer swap returns success: R3 removed already-applied recognition; the same oracle failed at False versus True. Restoring it passed.
claims: boundary "a late upload cannot replace the newer cache entry or retain its losing blob" at replace_value() via guard "test_stale_upload_cannot_replace_a_newer_entry"
boundary "repeating an already-installed pointer swap returns success" at replace_value() via guard "test_stale_upload_cannot_replace_a_newer_entry"

declaration.subject: posthog/query_cache/size_tracker.py
declaration.because: Two asynchronous uploads can complete out of order for one cache key. The Redis compare-and-swap and upload cleanup form the bounded publication contract.

parameters.operation identity: The per-upload UUID embedded in the S3 pointer
parameters.supersession relation: Current Redis bytes differ from the inline bytes captured by this upload
parameters.acceptance precondition: Current bytes equal expected inline bytes, or already equal this operation's pointer
parameters.cleanup ownership: A losing upload deletes its own blob, never the winner's blob

declaration.excludes: ABA with equal inline bytes, Redis failover, real S3 behavior and crash cleanup. R3 mutation failed first on orphan count; the later newer-response assertion was not reached.
declaration.falsifier: Store older then newer results; finish newer upload before older; observe two remaining blobs instead of one or read back the older response.

definition.title: Supersession safety
definition.promise: Late work publishes only while its declared precondition still holds; it cannot displace a superseding accepted value or clean up that winner's resources.
definition.appliesWhen: Asynchronous operations compete to publish state at one subject.
definition.excludes: General linearizability and equal-value intermediate-write detection unless explicitly represented by the precondition.
definition.falsifier: Finish a newer upload first, then an older upload, and observe an obsolete publication or surviving losing resource contrary to the cleanup policy.
definition.demoteWhen: A second context requires changing the supersession relation's meaning or hides the entire publication policy in an opaque predicate.

distinctFrom.because: Competing operations must not win late; the same already-applied operation must still recognize its own success.

example.limit: Removing the mismatch refusal fails on two remaining fake-storage objects. The later newer-response assertion is not reached in that mutant. Real Redis, controlled uploads, fake S3.

observation.detail: a late upload cannot replace the newer cache entry or retain its losing blob @ replace_value() (source-property guard)

declaration.subject: posthog/query_cache/size_tracker.py
declaration.because: A swap whose reply was lost must not be mistaken for a superseded upload: that result would select cleanup of the live pointer's blob.

parameters.operation identity: The unique pointer bytes for one upload
parameters.already-applied witness: Current Redis bytes equal the proposed pointer
parameters.retry horizon: While those pointer bytes remain the current entry
parameters.success result: TeamCacheSizeTracker.replace_value returns True even when expected inline bytes no longer match
parameters.cleanup consequence: Success avoids the losing-upload cleanup branch; the oracle directly checks return value and retained pointer

declaration.excludes: An actual lost network reply, real S3 retry cleanup, arbitrary duplicate execution or reuse of an operation identity.
declaration.falsifier: Publish a pointer, repeat replace_value with stale expected bytes, and observe False instead of True.

definition.title: Already-applied retry recognition
definition.promise: Repeating an operation whose own effect already landed recognizes that success rather than classifying the retry as a conflicting operation.
definition.appliesWhen: Replies can be lost and the caller retries a distinguishable operation.
definition.excludes: Exactly-once execution, detection of every network failure, and retry identities reused by unrelated operations.
definition.falsifier: Install an operation's pointer, repeat its swap with the old expected bytes, and receive a conflict result that would trigger losing-upload cleanup.
definition.demoteWhen: The implementation cannot identify its own prior effect independently of a coincidentally equal foreign effect.

distinctFrom.because: Recognizing success may permit redelivery; suppressing every retry can instead lose unfinished downstream work.

example.limit: Deleting already-applied recognition fails on False versus True at the retry assertion. No actual lost network reply was injected.

observation.detail: repeating an already-installed pointer swap returns success @ replace_value() (source-property guard)
